items.title: The Sequence Robotics - Issue #922: Learning About LeRobot: The Transformers Moment for Robots
items.summary: Robotics is experiencing a "Transformers moment" with a coordinated effort called LeRobot. Previously, robot learning suffered from fragmented setups, with each lab using incompatible datasets, rigs, and training loops. LeRobot's approach shifts the focus from model-centric learning to coordination-limited learning, similar to how Hugging Face shipped a protocol instead of just a model. This library has become the default substrate for open robot learning, drawing support from organizations like NVIDIA. Essentially, LeRobot aims to provide a unified framework for robot learning by shipping a protocol rather than just a model.
items.audio_script: From TheSequence, The Sequence Robotics - Issue 922: Learning About LeRobot: The Transformers Moment for Robots reports on a coordinated effort called LeRobot and its significance in the field of robot learning. LeRobot shifts the focus from model-centric learning to coordination-limited learning, establishing a unified framework for robot learning. The methodology involves creating a library that functions as a protocol for robot learning, similar to how other large-scale models offer standardized interfaces. This framework aims to overcome previous fragmentation caused by incompatible datasets and training loops across different research labs. LeRobot draws support from organizations including NVIDIA to become the default substrate for open robot learning. This unified approach provides a standardized method for developing and sharing robot learning models. The development indicates a path toward more cohesive and interoperable advancements in artificial intelligence for robotics.

items.title: Video Friday: Meet Microduck
items.summary: Video Friday features robotics videos and a calendar of upcoming robotics events. A robot named Microduck is introduced, a 25 cm device capable of walking, falling, and learning new tricks. Microduck is equipped with various sensors and is open-source, allowing for diverse interactive behaviors. Other featured topics include fish-inspired robots, lightweight grippers, and emotionally expressive locomotion in robots. The content also highlights advancements in robot autonomy and task execution.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Meet Microduck" introduces a small robot capable of dynamic movement and learning. This segment details the introduction of Microduck, a twenty-five centimeter device engineered to walk, fall, and acquire new behaviors through the use of various sensors. The robot is open-source, which facilitates diverse interactive behaviors, and its design incorporates advancements in robotics, alongside features such as fish-inspired robots, lightweight grippers, and emotionally expressive locomotion. Further content addresses advancements in robot autonomy and task execution capabilities within the field. These developments indicate continued progression in the development of adaptable and intelligent robotic systems.
